description: A package that reads navigator and document while it loads (dom-reader) makes the package that imports it (registering-plugin) one whose per-file evaluation by Jest shows: the plugin registers an entry id into a module-level registry (entry-registry, reached through the re-export entry-registry-barrel) while it loads, and the registry throws on an id it already holds. A third package (core-lib) is imported by the plugin and by a package with no per-file read (plain-widget), and notes each evaluation in core-lib-loads.txt. Three files on one worker under jest-environment-jsdom, each importing the registry, the widget and the plugin in that order (the package names keep that order under the import sorting): in each the entry is registered once, is an instance of the registry’s Entry, and the plugin and the widget see one core-lib. Jest evaluates every module per file, so core-lib-loads.txt holds one line per file. The PASS lines are not kept: the order of three files of one size varies between runs.

entry-registry-barrel.index.js:
// Re-exports the registry, as a package's sub-entry does.
module.exports = require('entry-registry')

plain-widget.index.js:
// A package that imports core-lib and nothing per file.
exports.core = require('core-lib')
